subject: EU AI Act / NIST RMF: readiness questions + eval sampling approach
messages:
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditech.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@meditech.com
Date: 2027-04-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications on EU AI Act classification + sampling for regression tests

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the initial materials you sent last week. We're putting together the final RFP package for our compliance committee and need a few clarifications before the packet goes to procurement. High-level asks:

1) EU AI Act: can you confirm whether Redwood considers your hosted text-generation endpoints "high-risk" for medical triage/decision support use cases, and what controls you recommend if a customer chooses to classify their integration as high-risk?

2) NIST AI RMF: we need a one-page mapping that shows which controls you provide (detect, respond, govern). You mentioned a mapping in the call but we need the artifact and the short explanations for each mapping point.

3) Regression sampling: our security reviewers want to see how you choose samples for eval/regression when a new model version is rolled out that affects clinical prompts. Specifically: population sampling strategy, size estimates, and how you detect semantic regressions vs. cosmetic changes.

Can you provide short answers and any artifacts by EOD Tuesday (US time)? Attachments referencing SOC2 or other audit artifacts would be appreciated.

Best,
Sam
Sam Ortiz
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Meditech Health
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on EU AI Act classification + sampling for regression tests

Sam,

Thanks — understood. Short answers below and we'll follow up with the artifacts attached. Laura and Monica are looping in details on the mapping and sampling plan.

1) EU AI Act classification: Redwood does not "classify" customers' use cases. We provide the controls and evidence to enable customers to operate in high-risk contexts. For medical triage: if a customer is using Redwood to influence clinical decisions, that usage may be considered high-risk under the EU AI Act. In that case we recommend (a) explicit contractual carve-outs and SLA terms, (b) model version pinning + canary rollouts with a blocking policy, (c) increased audit logging and retention, (d) human-in-the-loop gating for final decisions. We can provide a checklist customers can use to demonstrate operational mitigations.

2) NIST AI RMF mapping: attached is a compact mapping (redwood_nist_rm_mapping_v2.pdf) that maps Redwood product features to Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Govern across technical and organizational controls. High level: identity & asset inventory (model catalog + provenance), protect (tokenization, VPC private), detect (anomaly tracing, drift monitors), respond (rollback + alerting + canary policies), govern (role-based access, audit logs, artifact retention). Document includes references to concrete config options.

3) Regression sampling approach: see the attached spreadsheet (eval_sampling_plan_2027.xlsx) — summary: sampling is workload-driven. We take a stratified sample across: prompt families (by intent), user cohorts, and prior-failure buckets. For high-risk customers we recommend a two-tier approach: a targeted regression set (customer-supplied prompts + golden set) and a population sample sized to get ~95% confidence for x% change detection (spreadsheet shows example sizes). Semantic regressions detected via ensemble metrics (semantic similarity delta, hallucination score, safety signal changes) and by human raters for flagged cases. Monica added specifics below.

Attaching model_card_v3.md and a SOC2 summary for procurement. If you'd like, we can propose a brief playbook for customer-run canary + automatic rollback for high-risk deployments.

I'll leave the technical details to Laura/Monica.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditech.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-23T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on EU AI Act classification + sampling for regression tests

Sam — adding the technical appendix and a few concrete examples from our eval system. See attached files and the bullets below.

- NIST mapping highlights: for Detect we provide token-level latency/trace logs, per-request model-version tag, and drift detectors for top-k token distributions. For Respond we surface automated canary fail-open/fail-closed toggles and one-click rollback to prior model snapshot. For Govern we export immutable audit logs (WORM) and integration hooks for external KMS/HSM.

- Sampling methodology (summary):
  * Step 1: Identify customer-critical intents (customer provides up to 250 prompts or we extract from production logs).
  * Step 2: Construct stratified buckets: by intent, by expected response length, and by safety-signal history.
  * Step 3: Run A/B batch eval across new vs. old model using both automatic metrics and a human rater panel for any flagged deltas > threshold.
  * Step 4: Produce a regression report with pass/fail gates tied to rollout policy.

- Semantic vs cosmetic: we treat cosine similarity of embeddings + calibrated hallucination score as primary signals for semantic changes; prompt/response formatting diffs are flagged as cosmetic and measured separately. Thresholds are configurable per-customer.

Attachments: redwood_nist_rm_mapping_v2.pdf (mapping + short evidence items), eval_sampling_plan_2027.xlsx (sample sizes and example calculations), model_card_v3.md (model provenance + quantization/ops notes).

Let us know any examples or prompts you want us to include in the targeted regression set — we can import them into the spreadsheet and run a dry A/B within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarifications on EU AI Act classification + sampling for regression tests

Laura / Vivek — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups from our compliance team:

- Data residency & logs: for audit we need logs retained for 7 years. What retention tiers do you offer and are logs exportable to our SIEM?
- Human rater evidence: can you provide an example human-rater rubric you use for semantic regressions (we need to show the committee how disagreements are resolved)?
- SLA/rollback guarantees: for high-risk uses, procurement wants clarity on whether Redwood will enforce automatic rollback thresholds or whether that's customer-controlled.

If you can include short answers and a sample rubric by Monday morning, we can move to procurement for contract language.

Sam
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@meditech.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on EU AI Act classification + sampling for regression tests

Hi Sam — delivering the requested clarifications below and including two short artifacts inline. The attached SOC2 summary and model card were shared earlier.

1) Logs & retention: Redwood supports tiered retention. Standard (90 days), Extended (1 year), and Archive (configurable up to 10 years in compliance tier). For EU-regulated customers we offer log export to customer-owned S3 endpoints inside their VPC and direct SIEM integration via syslog/HTTPS. We'll include export instructions in the contract addendum.

2) Human-rater rubric (summary):
  - Task: rate semantic correctness on a 1-5 scale where 5 = Fully correct and actionable, 3 = partially correct with missing context, 1 = incorrect or harmful.
  - Disagreement resolution: two independent raters first; if scores differ by >=2, a third senior rater adjudicates. Final pass/fail gate defined by customer thresholds (e.g., mean >=4.2).
  - Safety overlay: any response flagged for safety (harmful content, PII leakage) automatically fails and enters an incident workflow.

3) SLA and rollback: our standard behavior is customer-controlled rollouts with Redwood providing canary tooling and automatic alerting. For customers operating in high-risk contexts we offer a managed option: Redwood can operate an automated rollback policy tied to regression gates (mutually agreed thresholds). That managed rollback option is part of the Dedicated/Private contracts and will be listed as an opt-in in the SOW.

Action items we propose:
  - Redwood to populate the targeted regression set with Meditech-supplied prompts (we can take an initial 200 prompts) and run a dry A/B within 48 hours of receipt.
  - Deliver final artifact pack (mapping PDF, sampling spreadsheet with Meditech rows, example rubric) as attachments for procurement.
  - Draft contract addendum language for log export + retention and managed rollback option.

If that works, I'll attach the populated spreadsheet and we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk procurement through the addendum.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_nist_rm_mapping_v2.pdf, eval_sampling_plan_2027.xlsx, model_card_v3.md, soc2-summary.pdf
